page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.s2.small is an entry-tier virtual server instance belonging to the ecs.s2 family. Built on the x86_64 architecture and managed via the KVM hypervisor, the instance delivers two dedicated virtual CPU cores paired with 2.0 GB of system memory. This configuration yields a tight ratio of 1.0 GB of memory per core, positioning the instance toward workloads with moderate computation requirements that do not demand extensive RAM footprint.

Hardware resource provisions for this instance exclude integrated local storage and GPU acceleration, meaning all persistent disk storage must be provisioned independently via network-attached cloud storage volumes. Furthermore, the instance provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses and does not include advanced hardware extensions such as AVX vector processing or hardware crypto offloading. The dedicated core allocation ensures that compute cycles remain steady and unthrottled without hypervisor credit contention.

From an operational and cost-efficiency perspective, the minimal resource footprint provides a straightforward entry point for lightweight compute operations without overpaying for unused memory or specialized hardware. The 1:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio presents distinct limitations for in-memory databases or multi-threaded memory-heavy services. Typical workloads suited for ecs.s2.small include lightweight background tasks, batch script runners, edge proxies, utility microservices, and development or testing environments requiring consistent compute access.
